name: Eltanin
description: A giant of type K5 III 47.3 parsecs away, 51.8 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 164058: radius 51.8 +/- 0.26 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 10.19 +/- 0.015 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 164058: effective temperature 3964 +/- 34 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 164058: log g 1.64, from Prugniel et al. (2011), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 4)

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 87833: RV -27.91 +/- 0.19 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 164058: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 21.14 +/- 0.1 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A giant of type K5 III, 47 parsecs away: 51.8 times the Sun's width and 598 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 10.19 milliarcseconds, which gives 51.8 solar radii and 3,964 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 164058: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff
